name: GNOME Terminal
summary: GNOME's long-time default terminal (VTE, GTK3). Settings live in dconf, not in a file: profiles with palette, font, cursor, line spacing, custom command, and global tab/headerbar options. No opacity, blur, images, splits or padding. Newer distros (Fedora 41+, Ubuntu 25.10+, per distro reports) ship Ptyxis instead.

linux.notes: There is NO config file to write: all settings are dconf keys, so the engine's file staging does not apply. Change them with `gsettings set` or `dconf write`/`dconf load`, and only after the user approves the plan. Back up first with `dconf dump /org/gnome/terminal/legacy/ > backup.ini` (restore: `dconf load /org/gnome/terminal/legacy/ < backup.ini`). Profile keys are on a relocatable schema, so every profile command needs the full form: gsettings set org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Profile:/org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:UUID/ KEY VALUE, where UUID comes from `gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.ProfilesList default` (strip the quotes). Global keys use org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Settings. Requires a running dconf/D-Bus session; from SSH or a root shell the commands change nothing for the desktop user. Ptyxis (GNOME's newer terminal, default on recent Fedora/Ubuntu releases) is a different app with schema org.gnome.Ptyxis and its own .palette files; it is NOT covered by this entry (see Ptyxis notes in the profiles capability).

ligatures.notes: No ligature key in the schema (enable-shaping is Arabic shaping only). Use kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty or iTerm2.

font-fallback.notes: No fallback list; Pango/fontconfig supplies fallback glyphs. Use a patched Nerd Font as the main font, or install a symbols font system-wide.

opacity.notes: The profile schema has no transparency key; the GNOME wiki FAQ says the option was removed from Preferences in 3.7. Ptyxis has a per-profile `opacity` key (org.gnome.Ptyxis.Profile, 0.0-1.0), or use kitty/WezTerm/Konsole/Alacritty.

blur.notes: No blur. Use Konsole, kitty, WezTerm or iTerm2.

background-image.notes: No background image. Use Konsole, kitty, WezTerm or iTerm2.

padding.notes: No padding key in the schema. Workaround: GTK CSS in ~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css targeting VteTerminal padding (unverified here), or choose another terminal.

splits.notes: No split panes. Use tmux/zellij, or Ptyxis/Konsole.

quake.notes: No drop-down mode. GNOME users use the Guake or Tilix terminals, or a Shell extension.

startup-layout.notes: No layout or session file. gnome-terminal(1) accepts per-launch options (such as --tab, --window, --working-directory and profile selection; not re-read here), or use tmux/zellij.
